subject.title: fix(security): suppress acknowledged audit findings without false positives

question: Should OpenClaw fully suppress hooks.request_session_key_enabled when hooks.allowedSessionKeyPrefixes has at least one non-blank prefix, or should prefix-constrained request session keys remain visible as an info or warning finding?
rationale: The implementation is small and source-aligned, but it changes security-audit output for externally supplied hook session keys; automation cannot decide the acceptable audit signal level.

options.title: Accept prefix-bound suppression
options.body: Land the PR as-is if secops agrees that non-empty allowedSessionKeyPrefixes removes the arbitrary-shape risk this finding reports.

options.title: Keep a lower-severity signal
options.body: Ask the contributor to retain an info-level or warning-level constrained-override finding if operators should still see bounded external session-key choice.

options.title: Defer to broader audit policy
options.body: Pause this PR if maintainers want this hook-prefix decision handled with the remaining audit suppression, model heuristic, and proxy-warning topics.

recommendation.title: Accept prefix-bound suppression
recommendation.body: Land the PR as-is if secops agrees that non-empty allowedSessionKeyPrefixes removes the arbitrary-shape risk this finding reports.

likelyOwner.reason: The touched code and docs are security-codeowned, and the unresolved choice is the security-audit boundary.
